author: Ifmyante
text:
xmzhang wrote: I was stopped out
 of an trade that I took yesterday, the setup looked very good, I've
applied everything I've learned here to this setup, but the bastard
stopped me out. Do you see any flaws in my setup, or is it just one of
those trades that just didn't work out.

Hiya

A QM must always be treated as a possible Diamond in the making, meaning
 that stops must be not just beyond the high/low, but beyond the FL the
H/L is a reaction to.

Also, you have your QM marked in an area of Supply. Is that supply itself a reaction to a FL? This question also is vital

author: Ifmyante
text:
milkeyway wrote: Hi IF.

I am currently practicing reading seasons on my mt4. But whenever swing
ends and takes turn, I wonder why i will take that trade or why I didn't
 take that trade. So, is it necessary to enter trade every turn of every
 end of the swing ? I hope not. It may not necessary to trade each
swing.

If price reaches its target and then engulfs back in, a reversal has
occurred - price will now have a target within the pole that took it to
where it turned, so why not trade it back to that TG? If it's not the
ultimate target which has been hit (PA in an HTF has told you that it
has further to go), and you only like to trade the big moves in the
HTFs, then there's no need to take the definite pips on offer here, as
it obviously isn't part of your trade plan

author: Jambowlyai
text:
Hey If, simply out of curiosity, have you ever looked back at
historical charts say from 100 years ago and seen if the market was
working the exact same way back then? It would be interesting to know
how long these shenanigans have been going on. I wonder if computers,
high frequency trading etc have forced the ITs to shift their tactics
throughout the ages. I've taken a peek myself but don't quite "get it"
yet so can't really conclude anything. Just wondering about your
thoughts on the topic.

author: geejay
text:
Jambowlyai - Here is a chart from S&P500 from 2000 - the last major market top (not 100 years I know).

I see some familiar price structures. I did not mark them all. I think
that the answer is likely yes. But I don't know how you would use this
info to make you a better trader. In other words, apart from an
intellectual discussion, how does knowing how the ITs behave a
generation ago help you today? Just thinking out loud.

GJ

author: Jambowlyai
text:
It is purely just a curiosity, intellectual discussion thing. Won't help trading a bit as far as I can see.

The answer would lead to different thoughts, none of which would have any benefit for trading either.

Okay, now back to saturating my brain with charts and fakeouts and ftrs
and engulfs in the hopes of forcing a breakthrough. Then maybe I can
answer my own question.
